           Compliance Filing in Response to June 5 Order

Dear Secretary Reese,

       Pursuant the order issued on June 5, 2026,1 by the Federal Energy Regulatory
Commission (“Commission”), Southwest Power Pool, Inc. (“SPP”) submits this
compliance filing to revise its Open Access Transmission Tariff (“Tariff”).2 SPP requests
an effective date of July 1, 2026, consistent with the effective date granted in the June 5
Order.

I.     BACKGROUND

       On February 10, 2026, SPP submitted revisions to its Tariff to add the proposed
Conditional High Impact Large Load Service (“CHILLS”) that will allow High Impact
Large Loads (“HILL”) to be served with non-firm conditional transmission service.3 On
March 30, 2026, the Commission issued a letter requesting additional information

II.    DISCUSSION OF TARIFF REVISIONS AND SPP COMPLIANCE

paragraph 92 of the June 5 Order:

              Attachment BA, to an Eligible Customer when it first submits a Completed
              Application for CHILLS pursuant to the Tariff at the completion of the
              studies outlined in Attachments AQ, AX, BA, and/or BC. Transactions
              under this CHILLSA will be arranged pursuant to Attachment BA.
              Executed Service Agreements that contain the information required under
              the Tariff will be filed with the Commission in compliance with applicable
              Commission regulations.7

include the applicable Schedule 11 subregional charge in compliance with paragraph 100

        In paragraph 92 of the Commission’s Order, the Commission directed SPP to make

       SPP proposes the following revisions to Section 2.22.2 of Attachment AE in

       D.      Attachment BA Addendum 1

               For instances where both Network Load and CHILLS load are located at

               excess hourly generation above the CHILLS Reserved Capacity to (1) add
               the hourly output of any Behind-The-Meter Generation that is located on
               the Network Load side of the Network Integration Transmission Service
               (“NITS”) meter and is not behind a CHILLS meter, and (2) subtract the
               positive (inflow, or CHILLS load) or negative (outflow) amount registered
               on any CHILLS meter located behind the NITS meter. Such excess hourly
               generation will be calculated as the minimum of the CHILLS load and the
               CHILLS Reserved Capacity, plus the hourly generation amount, less the

       F.      Attachment BC Section 2.2

        In paragraph 95 of the June 5 Order, the Commission directed SPP to make a
compliance filing to revise Section 2.2 of Attachment BC to align with its explanation in
the Deficiency Response. SPP’s Deficiency Response clarified that “[i]f the Transmission
Customer is taking both firm service or CHILLS at the same delivery point, the firm load
and CHILLS load must be separately metered. As the delivery point will be able to be
served by a combination of firm or CHILLS service, an entity may be required to execute
a service agreement under Attachment AQ, Attachment AX, and/or Attachment BA.”

        Because SPP may conduct multiple combinations of studies using Attachments
AQ, AX, BA, and BC, the specific combination of which will be driven by the situation
and needs of each Transmission Customer or Network Customer, SPP proposes to describe
the requirement by referring to the need for a Service Agreement instead of referring to the
individual study process attachments. This proposed revision simplifies the language and
retains the initial intent, which is that a HILL delivery point is not established without an
effective Service Agreement pursuant to Parts II, III, and/or VII of the Tariff, as applicable.
This revision clarifies that an effective Service Agreement is a necessary step for
establishing the HILL delivery point. Furthermore, this revised language is consistent with
the Deficiency Response in that more than one Service Agreement may be necessary if the
load at a single HILL delivery point is served by a combination of firm transmission service
and CHILLS.

44.3   Service Agreements:

       The Transmission Provider will offer a standard form Conditional High Impact Large
Load Service Agreement (CHILLSA), Addendum 2 to Attachment BA, to an Eligible Customer
when it first submits a Completed Application for CHILLS pursuant to the Tariffat the
completion of the studies outlined in Attachments AQ, AX, BA, and/or BC. Transactions under
this CHILLSA will be arranged pursuant to Attachment BA. Executed Service Agreements that
contain the information required under the Tariff will be filed with the Commission in
compliance with applicable Commission regulations.
 44.4    Classification of Conditional High Impact Large Load Service:

       CHILLS will be offered under terms and conditions contained in Part VII                    and
Attachment BA of the Tariff. The Transmission Provider and Transmission Owners undertake
no obligation under the Tariff to plan the Transmission System in order to have sufficient
capacity for CHILLS. Parties requesting CHILLS for the transmission of energy do so with the
full realization that such service is subject to availability and to Curtailment or Interruption under
the terms of the Tariff. The Transmission Customer or Network Customer will be billed for its
CHILLS Reserved Capacity under the terms of Schedules 11 and 15. The Transmission
Customer or the Network Customer must not withdraw energy from the Transmission System at
the CHILL delivery point that exceeds its CHILLS Reserved Capacity. The Transmission
Customer or the Network Customer must fully respond to a load shed or curtailment for the
CHILL delivery point directive by the Transmission Provider as described in Section 48 of the
Tariff. In the event that a Transmission Customer exceeds its CHILLS Reserved Capacity
amount at any Point of Delivery, the Transmission Customer or Network Customer must pay the
following penalty (in addition to the charges for all of the CHILLS capacity used): 100% of the
Non-Firm Point-To-Point Transmission Service charges under Schedules 8 and 11 for the
duration of the period when the additional service was used as specified below during the month
for the amount in excess of such capacity reservation. An excess of one hour or less will be
billed at the charge for weekday deliveries. Repeated daily use of unreserved capacity within a
seven-day period will increase the duration of the period to a weekly duration and multiple
instances of unreserved use during more than one seven-day period during a calendar month will
increase the duration of the period to a monthly duration. The Transmission Provider will
compensate the Transmission Owners for 100% of the (i) CHILLS charge, (ii) Subregional
Charge, (ii)(iii) Base Plan Zonal Charge, and (iii)(iv) Region-wide Charge for the period for
which they have provided service. The penalty revenues in excess of the amount distributed to
Transmission Owners will be used to reduce the Schedule 1-A1 charges collected by the
Transmission Provider from the Transmission Customers and Network Customers.                      All
Transmission Customers and Network Customers, except the penalized Transmission Customer
or Network Customer, will receive a reduction of Schedule 1-A1 charges pursuant to this section.
Such penalty revenues will be distributed by the Transmission Provider to Transmission
Customers and Network Customers pro-rata based on each entity’s monthly Schedule 1-A1
 charge, except for the penalized Transmission Customer or Network Customer, for the next
billing period ending at least 15 calendar days after the date the Transmission Provider collects
the penalty revenues from the penalized Transmission Customer or Network Customer. For the
amounts exceeding the CHILLS capacity reservation, the Transmission Customer or Network
Customer must purchase losses pursuant to Section 45.4.
                                SCHEDULE 15
                CONDITIONAL HIGH IMPACT LARGE LOAD SERVICE

        For each Point of Delivery of the Conditional High Impact Large Load Service
(“CHILLS”), the Transmission Customer and Network Customer must compensate the
Transmission Provider for the CHILLS up to the monthly sum of the applicable charges set forth
below in addition to other applicable charges specified in the Tariff. All effective rates under
this schedule will be posted in the Revenue Requirements and Rates File (“RRR File”) on the
SPP website.


       1.     Zonal Rates per Kilowatt: The Transmission Customer and Network Customer
must pay the zonal rate (per kilowatt) based upon the Zone where the load is located for the
CHILLS. The zonal rate will be the hourly rate applicable to Non-Firm Point-To-Point
Transmission Service for the specific on-peak or off-peak hour of the CHILLS usage. For each
hour without Curtailment, the hourly charge will be calculated using kilowatts of the CHILLS
Reserved Capacity. For each hour with Curtailment, the hourly charge will be calculated using
the Curtailment kilowatt limit specified by the Transmission Provider. CHILLS load exceeding
the Curtailment limit specified by the Transmission Provider or the CHILLS Reserved Capacity
is subject to additional charges and penalties pursuant to Part VII, Section 44.4 of this Tariff.

       The Zones are as follows:
Zone 1: American Electric Power – West
Zone 2: Kansas City Board of Public Utilities
Zone 3: City Utilities of Springfield, Missouri
Zone 4: Empire District Electric Company
Zone 5: Grand River Dam Authority
Zone 6: Evergy Metro, Inc.
Zone 7: Oklahoma Gas & Electric Company
Zone 8: Midwest Energy, Inc.
Zone 9: Evergy Missouri West, Inc.
Zone 10: Southwestern Power Administration
Zone 11: Southwestern Public Service
Zone 12: Sunflower Electric Power Corporation
Zone 13: Western Farmers Electric Cooperative
 Zone 14: Evergy Kansas Central, Inc. (Evergy Kansas Central, Inc. and Evergy Kansas South,
         Inc.)
Zone 15: Reserved for Future Use
Zone 16: Lincoln Electric System
Zone 17: Nebraska Public Power District
Zone 18: Omaha Public Power District
Zone 19: Upper Missouri Zone
No changes in Zones will be made without submitting a filing to the Commission.


       2.    Caps: The total demand charge in any month for usage up to the CHILLS
Reserved Capacity will not exceed the monthly rate times the amount in kilowatts of CHILLS
Reserved Capacity in such month.


       3.     Redispatch Costs: The redispatch costs will be calculated in accordance with the
formula and protocols shown in Attachment K.


        4.     Discounts: The Transmission Provider may offer discounts under this
Schedule. Three principal requirements apply to discounts for transmission service as
follows: (1) any offer of a discount made by the Transmission Provider must be announced to all
Eligible Customers solely by posting on the OASIS, (2) any customer-initiated requests for
discounts must occur solely by posting on the OASIS, and (3) once a discount is negotiated,
details must be immediately posted on the OASIS. For any discount agreed upon for service to a
Point(s) of Delivery, the Transmission Provider must offer the same discounted CHILLS rate for
the same time period to all Eligible Customers on all unconstrained transmission paths that go to
the same Point(s) of Delivery on the Transmission System. In offering discounts, the
Transmission Provider’s goal will be to maximize transmission revenues.

       45.     Real Power Losses: The Transmission Customer and Network Customer will be
responsible for real power losses determined in accordance with Attachment M and Part VII,
Section 45.4 of this Tariff.


       56.     Wholesale Distribution Service: Where Wholesale Distribution Service is
provided to effectuate CHILLS, the Transmission Customer and Network Customer must pay all
charges levied pursuant to the Wholesale Distribution Service Agreement and Schedule 10.
        67.     Base Plan Zonal Charges, Subregional Charge, and Region-wide
Charges: The Transmission Customer and Network Customer must pay the applicable Schedule
11 zonal rate (per kilowatt) based upon the Zone where the load is located, the applicable
Schedule 11 Subregional Charge (per kilowatt) based upon the Subregion where the load is
located, and the applicable Schedule 11 region-wide rate for CHILLS. The rates will be the
applicable point-to-point hourly rates for the specific on-peak or off-peak hour of CHILLS
usage. The hourly charges will be calculated using hourly kilowatts as stated in Section 1 of
Schedule 15. The total Schedule 11 zonal charge in any month for usage up to the CHILLS
Reserved Capacity will not exceed the Schedule 11 point-to-point zonal monthly rate times the
amount in kilowatts of CHILLS Reserved Capacity in such month. The total Schedule 11 region-
wide charge in any month for usage up to the CHILLS Reserved Capacity will not exceed the
Schedule 11 point-to-point region-wide rate times the amount of kilowatts of CHILLS Reserved
Capacity in such month.

       78.    Resales: Resales are not permissible for CHILLS.
 2.22.2 Resources Supporting a HILL or CHILL

(1)   The following applies to Resources supporting a CHILL:
      (a)    Resources supporting a CHILL must submit Resource Offers sufficient to cover
             forecasted withdrawals by the CHILL as described in the Protocols.
      (b)    When a Resource supports more than one CHILL, the Resource must be split, and
             it must be registered such that there are the same number of registered Resources
             as the number of CHILLs the facility is supporting.


(2)   Resources with Load Limited Resource Interconnection Service as defined in Attachment
      BB of the Tariff must:
      (a)    Follow all rules and restrictions included in their HILLGIA.
      (b)    Ensure the sum of the Maximum Economic Capacity Operating Limits of
             supporting Resources with Load Limited Resource Interconnection Service, as
             defined in Attachment BB of the Tariff, does not exceed the submitted HILL or
             CHILL load forecast value of the corresponding HILL or CHILL except when
             directed by the Transmission Provider to mitigate Emergency Conditions or as
             specified in the Resource’s generator interconnection agreement.


(3)   Behind-The-Meter Generation supporting a HILL, including any portion of a HILL
      which is a CHILL, and registered in the Integrated Marketplace must abide by the
      following rules:
      (a)    The load Meter Settlement Location associated with the Behind-The-Meter
             Generation must not have an injection into the Transmission System without
             appropriate transmission service;
      (b)    Submit a Day-Ahead and Real Time Balancing Market Offer where the Resource
             Maximum Normal, Economic, Regulation and Emergency Capacity Operating
             limit must not exceed the projected demand at that load Meter Settlement
             Location for an Operating Hour or Dispatch Interval, unless the Resource has
             appropriate transmission service.

or make changes in facilities at a HILL delivery point and the Network Customer or
Transmission Customer does not have enough existing Designated Resources or planned

generation capacity with an accreditation MW value, as determined pursuant to Attachment AA

Attachment BC, Host Transmission Owner is defined as the owner of that portion of the
Transmission System to which such connection or modification is to be made. The Network
Customer or Transmission Customer will submit a request for a HILL Delivery Point Limitations
Assessment (“HDPLA”) in writing to (a) the Transmission Provider and the Host Transmission
Owner as specified in Section 20 of the Network Operating Agreement or (b) the Transmission
Provider as specified in Section 8 of the Point-To-Point Transmission Service Agreement, as
applicable. Such request must contain as much information as is known or projected at the time
of the request as set forth in “Sample Request For a High Impact Large Load Delivery Point
Initial Assessment” attached hereto as Addendum 1. The delivery point must satisfy the HILL
requirements outlined in Attachment BA of this Tariff.
 2.0    Studies: The Transmission Provider and Host Transmission Owner will conduct all
necessary studies associated with the HILL delivery point changes.           Such studies will be
conducted at Network Customer’s or Transmission Customer’s expense pursuant to the
provisions of this section.

      2.1      HILL Load Connection Study: Host Transmission Owner must respond within
      ten (10) Business Days of receipt of such request and, if necessary, provide a HILL Load
      Connection Study (“HLCS”) agreement and a list of any additional information that Host
      Transmission Owner requires from the Network Customer or Transmission Customer in
      order to proceed with such study. Unless otherwise agreed, the HLCS agreement will
      commit the Network Customer or Transmission Customer to pay Host Transmission
      Owner the actual cost to complete the study. The Host Transmission Owner may require an
      advance deposit equal to the estimated study cost or $25,000, whichever is less. In

      modifying an existing HILL delivery point or establishing a new HILL delivery point using
      power flow and short circuit analyses and any other analyses that are appropriate. The Host

      necessary for establishing the requested delivery point and any system additions and
      upgrades needed to address any problems identified in the HLCS. There may be additional
      requirements pursuant to Attachment BA of this Tariff.


      If the Network Customer or Transmission Customer fails to return an executed HLCS
      agreement within thirty (30) Calendar Days of receipt along with the required deposit, or at
      a later date as the Parties mutually agree, Host Transmission Owner will deem the study
      request to be withdrawn. The Network Customer or Transmission Customer may withdraw
      its study request at any time by written notice of such withdrawal to the Host Transmission
      Owner and the Transmission Provider. Host Transmission Owner will complete the HLCS
      and issue a HILL Load Connection Report to the Transmission Customer and Transmission
      Provider by or before ninety (90) Calendar Days after receipt of an executed HLCS
      agreement, deposit and necessary data, or at a later date as the Parties mutually agree.


      Upon completion of the HLCS, the Network Customer or Transmission Customer must
 reimburse Host Transmission Owner for the unpaid cost of the HLCS if the cost of the
HLCS exceeds the deposit.       Host Transmission Owner must refund to the Network
Customer or Transmission Customer any portion of the deposit that exceeds the cost of the
HLCS with interest earned in the interest-bearing account in which Host Transmission
Owner has placed the deposit, or if such account does not exist, with interest calculated in
accordance with 18 C.F.R. § 35.19a(a)(2).


2.2       Transmission System Study: Upon receipt of the Request for a HDPLA, the
Transmission Provider will perform an assessment of the impact of the requested delivery
point configuration change on the Transmission System and, if requested by the Network
Customer or Transmission Customer, information detailing the limitations of the
Transmission System in supporting any Conditional High Impact Large Load Service. The
Transmission Provider will conclude its assessment and notify the Transmission Customer

megawatt amounts of requested transmission service of the HILL will be subject to the
HDPLA, described below, and to supplemental study requirements outlined in Section

assess the impacts on the Transmission System caused by requested HILL delivery point
additions or modifications due to the increased load using power flow, short circuit,
dynamics, and any other analyses that are appropriate.


The Transmission Provider will send a study report to the Transmission Customer and the

Transmission Customer and the Host Transmission Owner and provide an estimate of the
time needed to reach a final determination along with an explanation of the reason(s) that
additional time is required to complete the study. Upon completion of the HDPLA, the

HDPLA. The HDPLA study results do not establish a HILL delivery point without an

 the execution of a Service Agreement by the Transmission Customer or Network Customer

requires a Service Agreement pursuant to Part VII of the Tariff. for load that cannot be
served by currently planned generation and/or Designated Resources until after the
Transmission Customer or Network Customer executes a Service Agreement pursuant to
Attachment AQ, Attachment AX, or Attachment BA of the Tariff, for such load. The
HDPLA study results will expire one (1) year after issuance of the study report.

44.3   Service Agreements:

       The Transmission Provider will offer a standard form Conditional High Impact Large Load
Service Agreement (CHILLSA), Addendum 2 to Attachment BA, to an Eligible Customer at the
completion of the studies outlined in Attachments AQ, AX, BA, and/or BC. Transactions under
this CHILLSA will be arranged pursuant to Attachment BA. Executed Service Agreements that
contain the information required under the Tariff will be filed with the Commission in compliance
with applicable Commission regulations.
 44.4    Classification of Conditional High Impact Large Load Service:

       CHILLS will be offered under terms and conditions contained in Part VII and Attachment
BA of the Tariff. The Transmission Provider and Transmission Owners undertake no obligation
under the Tariff to plan the Transmission System in order to have sufficient capacity for CHILLS.
Parties requesting CHILLS for the transmission of energy do so with the full realization that such
service is subject to availability and to Curtailment or Interruption under the terms of the Tariff.
The Transmission Customer or Network Customer will be billed for its CHILLS Reserved
Capacity under the terms of Schedules 11 and 15. The Transmission Customer or the Network
Customer must not withdraw energy from the Transmission System at the CHILL delivery point
that exceeds its CHILLS Reserved Capacity. The Transmission Customer or the Network
Customer must fully respond to a load shed or curtailment for the CHILL delivery point directive
by the Transmission Provider as described in Section 48 of the Tariff. In the event that a
Transmission Customer exceeds its CHILLS Reserved Capacity amount at any Point of Delivery,
the Transmission Customer or Network Customer must pay the following penalty (in addition to
the charges for all of the CHILLS capacity used): 100% of the Non-Firm Point-To-Point
Transmission Service charges under Schedules 8 and 11 for the duration of the period when the
additional service was used as specified below during the month for the amount in excess of such
capacity reservation. An excess of one hour or less will be billed at the charge for weekday
deliveries. Repeated daily use of unreserved capacity within a seven-day period will increase the
duration of the period to a weekly duration and multiple instances of unreserved use during more
than one seven-day period during a calendar month will increase the duration of the period to a
monthly duration. The Transmission Provider will compensate the Transmission Owners for
100% of the (i) CHILLS charge, (ii) Subregional Charge, (iii) Base Plan Zonal Charge, and (iv)
Region-wide Charge for the period for which they have provided service. The penalty revenues
in excess of the amount distributed to Transmission Owners will be used to reduce the Schedule
1-A1 charges collected by the Transmission Provider from the Transmission Customers and
Network Customers. All Transmission Customers and Network Customers, except the penalized
Transmission Customer or Network Customer, will receive a reduction of Schedule 1-A1 charges
pursuant to this section. Such penalty revenues will be distributed by the Transmission Provider
to Transmission Customers and Network Customers pro-rata based on each entity’s monthly
Schedule 1-A1 charge, except for the penalized Transmission Customer or Network Customer, for
 the next billing period ending at least 15 calendar days after the date the Transmission Provider
collects the penalty revenues from the penalized Transmission Customer or Network Customer.
For the amounts exceeding the CHILLS capacity reservation, the Transmission Customer or
Network Customer must purchase losses pursuant to Section 45.4.
                                SCHEDULE 15
                CONDITIONAL HIGH IMPACT LARGE LOAD SERVICE

       For each Point of Delivery of the Conditional High Impact Large Load Service
(“CHILLS”), the Transmission Customer and Network Customer must compensate the
Transmission Provider for the CHILLS up to the monthly sum of the applicable charges set forth
below in addition to other applicable charges specified in the Tariff. All effective rates under this
schedule will be posted in the Revenue Requirements and Rates File (“RRR File”) on the SPP
website.


       1.     Zonal Rates per Kilowatt: The Transmission Customer and Network Customer
must pay the zonal rate (per kilowatt) based upon the Zone where the load is located for the
CHILLS. The zonal rate will be the hourly rate applicable to Non-Firm Point-To-Point
Transmission Service for the specific on-peak or off-peak hour of the CHILLS usage. For each
hour without Curtailment, the hourly charge will be calculated using kilowatts of the CHILLS
Reserved Capacity. For each hour with Curtailment, the hourly charge will be calculated using
the Curtailment kilowatt limit specified by the Transmission Provider. CHILLS load exceeding
the Curtailment limit specified by the Transmission Provider or the CHILLS Reserved Capacity is
subject to additional charges and penalties pursuant to Part VII, Section 44.4 of this Tariff.

No changes in Zones will be made without submitting a filing to the Commission.


       2.      Caps: The total demand charge in any month for usage up to the CHILLS Reserved
Capacity will not exceed the monthly rate times the amount in kilowatts of CHILLS Reserved
Capacity in such month.


       3.     Redispatch Costs: The redispatch costs will be calculated in accordance with the
formula and protocols shown in Attachment K.


        4.     Discounts: The Transmission Provider may offer discounts under this
Schedule. Three principal requirements apply to discounts for transmission service as
follows: (1) any offer of a discount made by the Transmission Provider must be announced to all
Eligible Customers solely by posting on the OASIS, (2) any customer-initiated requests for
discounts must occur solely by posting on the OASIS, and (3) once a discount is negotiated, details
must be immediately posted on the OASIS. For any discount agreed upon for service to a Point(s)
of Delivery, the Transmission Provider must offer the same discounted CHILLS rate for the same
time period to all Eligible Customers on all unconstrained transmission paths that go to the same
Point(s) of Delivery on the Transmission System. In offering discounts, the Transmission
Provider’s goal will be to maximize transmission revenues.

       5.      Real Power Losses: The Transmission Customer and Network Customer will be
responsible for real power losses determined in accordance with Attachment M and Part VII,
Section 45.4 of this Tariff.


       6.      Wholesale Distribution Service: Where Wholesale Distribution Service is
provided to effectuate CHILLS, the Transmission Customer and Network Customer must pay all
charges levied pursuant to the Wholesale Distribution Service Agreement and Schedule 10.
         7.      Base Plan Zonal Charges, Subregional Charge, and Region-wide Charges: The
Transmission Customer and Network Customer must pay the applicable Schedule 11 zonal rate
(per kilowatt) based upon the Zone where the load is located, the applicable Schedule 11
Subregional Charge (per kilowatt) based upon the Subregion where the load is located, and the
applicable Schedule 11 region-wide rate for CHILLS. The rates will be the applicable point-to-
point hourly rates for the specific on-peak or off-peak hour of CHILLS usage. The hourly charges
will be calculated using hourly kilowatts as stated in Section 1 of Schedule 15. The total Schedule
11 zonal charge in any month for usage up to the CHILLS Reserved Capacity will not exceed the
Schedule 11 point-to-point zonal monthly rate times the amount in kilowatts of CHILLS Reserved
Capacity in such month. The total Schedule 11 region-wide charge in any month for usage up to
the CHILLS Reserved Capacity will not exceed the Schedule 11 point-to-point region-wide rate
times the amount of kilowatts of CHILLS Reserved Capacity in such month.

       8.      Resales: Resales are not permissible for CHILLS.
 2.22.2 Resources Supporting a HILL or CHILL

(1)   The following applies to Resources supporting a CHILL:
      (a)    Resources supporting a CHILL must submit Resource Offers sufficient to cover
             forecasted withdrawals by the CHILL as described in the Protocols.
      (b)    When a Resource supports more than one CHILL, the Resource must be split, and

             CHILL load forecast value of the corresponding HILL or CHILL except when
             directed by the Transmission Provider to mitigate Emergency Conditions or as
             specified in the Resource’s generator interconnection agreement.


(3)   Behind-The-Meter Generation supporting a HILL, including any portion of a HILL which

      (a)    The load Meter Settlement Location associated with the Behind-The-Meter

 1.0    Requests for Establishment or Changes in High Impact Large Load (“HILL”) Local
Delivery Facilities: When it becomes necessary or desirable to establish a HILL delivery point
or make changes in facilities at a HILL delivery point and the Network Customer or Transmission
Customer does not have enough existing Designated Resources or planned Designated Resources
to serve the increased load plus losses, the provisions of this Attachment BC apply. However, the
Network Customer or Transmission Customer must have sufficient generation capacity with an
accreditation MW value, as determined pursuant to Attachment AA of the Tariff, that is sufficient
to cover the entire HILL, including losses. For the purposes of this Attachment BC, Host
Transmission Owner is defined as the owner of that portion of the Transmission System to which
such connection or modification is to be made. The Network Customer or Transmission Customer
will submit a request for a HILL Delivery Point Limitations Assessment (“HDPLA”) in writing to
the Transmission Provider and the Host Transmission Owner. Such request must contain as much
information as is known or projected at the time of the request as set forth in “Sample Request For
a High Impact Large Load Delivery Point Initial Assessment” attached hereto as Addendum 1.
The delivery point must satisfy the HILL requirements outlined in Attachment BA of this Tariff.
 2.0    Studies: The Transmission Provider and Host Transmission Owner will conduct all
necessary studies associated with the HILL delivery point changes. Such studies will be conducted
at Network Customer’s or Transmission Customer’s expense pursuant to the provisions of this
section.

      2.1      HILL Load Connection Study: Host Transmission Owner must respond within
      ten (10) Business Days of receipt of such request and, if necessary, provide a HILL Load
      Connection Study (“HLCS”) agreement and a list of any additional information that Host
      Transmission Owner requires from the Network Customer or Transmission Customer in
      order to proceed with such study. Unless otherwise agreed, the HLCS agreement will commit
      the Network Customer or Transmission Customer to pay Host Transmission Owner the
      actual cost to complete the study. The Host Transmission Owner may require an advance
      deposit equal to the estimated study cost or $25,000, whichever is less. In conducting the
      HLCS, the Host Transmission Owner will assess the feasibility of modifying an existing
      HILL delivery point or establishing a new HILL delivery point using power flow and short
      circuit analyses and any other analyses that are appropriate. The Host Transmission Owner
      will also determine the details and estimated cost of facilities necessary for establishing the
      requested delivery point and any system additions and upgrades needed to address any
      problems identified in the HLCS. There may be additional requirements pursuant to
      Attachment BA of this Tariff.


      If the Network Customer or Transmission Customer fails to return an executed HLCS
      agreement within thirty (30) Calendar Days of receipt along with the required deposit, or at
      a later date as the Parties mutually agree, Host Transmission Owner will deem the study
      request to be withdrawn. The Network Customer or Transmission Customer may withdraw
      its study request at any time by written notice of such withdrawal to the Host Transmission
      Owner and the Transmission Provider. Host Transmission Owner will complete the HLCS
      and issue a HILL Load Connection Report to the Transmission Customer and Transmission
      Provider by or before ninety (90) Calendar Days after receipt of an executed HLCS
      agreement, deposit and necessary data, or at a later date as the Parties mutually agree.


      Upon completion of the HLCS, the Network Customer or Transmission Customer must
 reimburse Host Transmission Owner for the unpaid cost of the HLCS if the cost of the HLCS
exceeds the deposit. Host Transmission Owner must refund to the Network Customer or
Transmission Customer any portion of the deposit that exceeds the cost of the HLCS with
interest earned in the interest-bearing account in which Host Transmission Owner has placed
the deposit, or if such account does not exist, with interest calculated in accordance with 18
C.F.R. § 35.19a(a)(2).


2.2       Transmission System Study: Upon receipt of the Request for a HDPLA, the
Transmission Provider will perform an assessment of the impact of the requested delivery
point configuration change on the Transmission System and, if requested by the Network
Customer or Transmission Customer, information detailing the limitations of the
Transmission System in supporting any Conditional High Impact Large Load Service. The
Transmission Provider will conclude its assessment and notify the Transmission Customer
of the findings. All HILLs without Designated Resources or planned generation for any
megawatt amounts of requested transmission service of the HILL will be subject to the
HDPLA, described below, and to supplemental study requirements outlined in Section
2.1.3.4 of Attachment BA of this Tariff. During the HDPLA, Transmission Provider will
assess the impacts on the Transmission System caused by requested HILL delivery point
additions or modifications due to the increased load using power flow, short circuit,
dynamics, and any other analyses that are appropriate.


The Transmission Provider will send a study report to the Transmission Customer and the
Host Transmission Owner within ninety (90) Calendar Days of all Parties agreeing to study
assumptions during the scoping call. If the Transmission Provider is unable to complete the
study within ninety (90) Calendar Days, the Transmission Provider will notify the
Transmission Customer and the Host Transmission Owner and provide an estimate of the
time needed to reach a final determination along with an explanation of the reason(s) that
additional time is required to complete the study. Upon completion of the HDPLA, the
Transmission Customer must reimburse the Transmission Provider for the cost of the
HDPLA. The HDPLA study results do not establish a HILL delivery point without an
effective Service Agreement. A requirement for establishment of a HILL delivery point is
 the execution of a Service Agreement by the Transmission Customer or Network Customer
for that delivery point or Commission approval of such a Service Agreement if filed
unexecuted. Any portion of the HILL delivery point load that is to be served with firm
transmission service requires a Service Agreement pursuant to Part II or Part III of the Tariff.
Any portion of the HILL delivery point load that is to be served with CHILLS requires a
Service Agreement pursuant to Part VII of the Tariff. The HDPLA study results will expire
one (1) year after issuance of the study report.

 44.4    Classification of Conditional High Impact Large Load Service:

       CHILLS will be offered under terms and conditions contained in Part VII and Attachment
BA of the Tariff. The Transmission Provider and Transmission Owners undertake no obligation
under the Tariff to plan the Transmission System in order to have sufficient capacity for CHILLS.
Parties requesting CHILLS for the transmission of energy do so with the full realization that such
service is subject to availability and to Curtailment or Interruption under the terms of the Tariff.
The Transmission Customer or Network Customer will be billed for its CHILLS Reserved
Capacity under the terms of Schedules 11 and 15. The Transmission Customer or the Network
Customer must not withdraw energy from the Transmission System at the CHILL delivery point
that exceeds its CHILLS Reserved Capacity. The Transmission Customer or the Network
Customer must fully respond to a load shed or curtailment for the CHILL delivery point directive
by the Transmission Provider as described in Section 48 of the Tariff. In the event that a
Transmission Customer exceeds its CHILLS Reserved Capacity amount at any Point of Delivery,
the Transmission Customer or Network Customer must pay the following penalty (in addition to
the charges for all of the CHILLS capacity used): 100% of the Non-Firm Point-To-Point
Transmission Service charges under Schedules 8 and 11 for the duration of the period when the
additional service was used as specified below during the month for the amount in excess of such
capacity reservation. An excess of one hour or less will be billed at the charge for weekday
deliveries. Repeated daily use of unreserved capacity within a seven-day period will increase the
duration of the period to a weekly duration and multiple instances of unreserved use during more
than one seven-day period during a calendar month will increase the duration of the period to a
monthly duration. The Transmission Provider will compensate the Transmission Owners for
100% of the (i) CHILLS charge, (ii) Subregional Charge, (iii) Base Plan Zonal Charge, and (iv)
Region-wide Charge for the period for which they have provided service. The penalty revenues in
excess of the amount distributed to Transmission Owners will be used to reduce the Schedule 1-A1
charges collected by the Transmission Provider from the Transmission Customers and Network
Customers.    All Transmission Customers and Network Customers, except the penalized
Transmission Customer or Network Customer, will receive a reduction of Schedule 1-A1 charges
pursuant to this section. Such penalty revenues will be distributed by the Transmission Provider to
Transmission Customers and Network Customers pro-rata based on each entity’s monthly
 Schedule 1-A1 charge, except for the penalized Transmission Customer or Network Customer, for
the next billing period ending at least 15 calendar days after the date the Transmission Provider
collects the penalty revenues from the penalized Transmission Customer or Network Customer.
For the amounts exceeding the CHILLS capacity reservation, the Transmission Customer or
Network Customer must purchase losses pursuant to Section 45.4.

                                SCHEDULE 15
                CONDITIONAL HIGH IMPACT LARGE LOAD SERVICE

       For each Point of Delivery of the Conditional High Impact Large Load Service
(“CHILLS”), the Transmission Customer and Network Customer must compensate the
Transmission Provider for the CHILLS up to the monthly sum of the applicable charges set forth
below in addition to other applicable charges specified in the Tariff. All effective rates under this
schedule will be posted in the Revenue Requirements and Rates File (“RRR File”) on the SPP
website.


        1.      Zonal Rates per Kilowatt: The Transmission Customer and Network Customer
must pay the zonal rate (per kilowatt) based upon the Zone where the load is located for the
CHILLS. The zonal rate will be the hourly rate applicable to Non-Firm Point-To-Point
Transmission Service for the specific on-peak or off-peak hour of the CHILLS usage. For each
hour without Curtailment, the hourly charge will be calculated using kilowatts of the CHILLS
Reserved Capacity. For each hour with Curtailment, the hourly charge will be calculated using the
Curtailment kilowatt limit specified by the Transmission Provider. CHILLS load exceeding the
Curtailment limit specified by the Transmission Provider or the CHILLS Reserved Capacity is
subject to additional charges and penalties pursuant to Part VII, Section 44.4 of this Tariff.


       The Zones are as follows:
Zone 1: American Electric Power – West
Zone 2: Kansas City Board of Public Utilities
Zone 3: City Utilities of Springfield, Missouri
Zone 4: Empire District Electric Company
Zone 5: Grand River Dam Authority
Zone 6: Evergy Metro, Inc.
Zone 7: Oklahoma Gas & Electric Company
Zone 8: Midwest Energy, Inc.
Zone 9: Evergy Missouri West, Inc.
Zone 10: Southwestern Power Administration
Zone 11: Southwestern Public Service
Zone 12: Sunflower Electric Power Corporation
Zone 13: Western Farmers Electric Cooperative
 Zone 14: Evergy Kansas Central, Inc. (Evergy Kansas Central, Inc. and Evergy Kansas South,
         Inc.)
Zone 15: Reserved for Future Use
Zone 16: Lincoln Electric System
Zone 17: Nebraska Public Power District
Zone 18: Omaha Public Power District
Zone 19: Upper Missouri Zone
No changes in Zones will be made without submitting a filing to the Commission.


       2.      Caps: The total demand charge in any month for usage up to the CHILLS Reserved
Capacity will not exceed the monthly rate times the amount in kilowatts of CHILLS Reserved
Capacity in such month.


       3.     Redispatch Costs: The redispatch costs will be calculated in accordance with the
formula and protocols shown in Attachment K.


        4.     Discounts: The Transmission Provider may offer discounts under this
Schedule. Three principal requirements apply to discounts for transmission service as
follows: (1) any offer of a discount made by the Transmission Provider must be announced to all
Eligible Customers solely by posting on the OASIS, (2) any customer-initiated requests for
discounts must occur solely by posting on the OASIS, and (3) once a discount is negotiated, details
must be immediately posted on the OASIS. For any discount agreed upon for service to a Point(s)
of Delivery, the Transmission Provider must offer the same discounted CHILLS rate for the same
time period to all Eligible Customers on all unconstrained transmission paths that go to the same
Point(s) of Delivery on the Transmission System. In offering discounts, the Transmission
Provider’s goal will be to maximize transmission revenues.


       5.      Real Power Losses: The Transmission Customer and Network Customer will be
responsible for real power losses determined in accordance with Attachment M and Part VII,
Section 45.4 of this Tariff.


       6.      Wholesale Distribution Service: Where Wholesale Distribution Service is
provided to effectuate CHILLS, the Transmission Customer and Network Customer must pay all
charges levied pursuant to the Wholesale Distribution Service Agreement and Schedule 10.
         7.      Base Plan Zonal Charges, Subregional Charge, and Region-wide Charges: The
Transmission Customer and Network Customer must pay the applicable Schedule 11 zonal rate
(per kilowatt) based upon the Zone where the load is located, the applicable Schedule 11
Subregional Charge (per kilowatt) based upon the Subregion where the load is located, and the
applicable Schedule 11 region-wide rate for CHILLS. The rates will be the applicable point-to-
point hourly rates for the specific on-peak or off-peak hour of CHILLS usage. The hourly charges
will be calculated using hourly kilowatts as stated in Section 1 of Schedule 15. The total Schedule
11 zonal charge in any month for usage up to the CHILLS Reserved Capacity will not exceed the
Schedule 11 point-to-point zonal monthly rate times the amount in kilowatts of CHILLS Reserved
Capacity in such month. The total Schedule 11 region-wide charge in any month for usage up to the
CHILLS Reserved Capacity will not exceed the Schedule 11 point-to-point region-wide rate times
the amount of kilowatts of CHILLS Reserved Capacity in such month.

       8.      Resales: Resales are not permissible for CHILLS.

 1.0    Requests for Establishment or Changes in High Impact Large Load (“HILL”) Local
Delivery Facilities: When it becomes necessary or desirable to establish a HILL delivery point or
make changes in facilities at a HILL delivery point and the Network Customer or Transmission
Customer does not have enough existing Designated Resources or planned Designated Resources
to serve the increased load plus losses, the provisions of this Attachment BC apply. However, the
Network Customer or Transmission Customer must have sufficient generation capacity with an
accreditation MW value, as determined pursuant to Attachment AA of the Tariff, that is sufficient
to cover the entire HILL, including losses. For the purposes of this Attachment BC, Host
Transmission Owner is defined as the owner of that portion of the Transmission System to which
such connection or modification is to be made. The Network Customer or Transmission Customer
will submit a request for a HILL Delivery Point Limitations Assessment (“HDPLA”) in writing to
the Transmission Provider and the Host Transmission Owner. Such request must contain as much
information as is known or projected at the time of the request as set forth in “Sample Request For a
High Impact Large Load Delivery Point Initial Assessment” attached hereto as Addendum 1. The
delivery point must satisfy the HILL requirements outlined in Attachment BA of this Tariff.

 2.0    Studies: The Transmission Provider and Host Transmission Owner will conduct all
necessary studies associated with the HILL delivery point changes. Such studies will be conducted
at Network Customer’s or Transmission Customer’s expense pursuant to the provisions of this
section.

      2.1      HILL Load Connection Study: Host Transmission Owner must respond within
      ten (10) Business Days of receipt of such request and, if necessary, provide a HILL Load
      Connection Study (“HLCS”) agreement and a list of any additional information that Host
      Transmission Owner requires from the Network Customer or Transmission Customer in
      order to proceed with such study. Unless otherwise agreed, the HLCS agreement will commit
      the Network Customer or Transmission Customer to pay Host Transmission Owner the
      actual cost to complete the study. The Host Transmission Owner may require an advance
      deposit equal to the estimated study cost or $25,000, whichever is less. In conducting the
      HLCS, the Host Transmission Owner will assess the feasibility of modifying an existing
      HILL delivery point or establishing a new HILL delivery point using power flow and short
      circuit analyses and any other analyses that are appropriate. The Host Transmission Owner
      will also determine the details and estimated cost of facilities necessary for establishing the
      requested delivery point and any system additions and upgrades needed to address any
      problems identified in the HLCS. There may be additional requirements pursuant to
      Attachment BA of this Tariff.


      If the Network Customer or Transmission Customer fails to return an executed HLCS
      agreement within thirty (30) Calendar Days of receipt along with the required deposit, or at a
      later date as the Parties mutually agree, Host Transmission Owner will deem the study
      request to be withdrawn. The Network Customer or Transmission Customer may withdraw
      its study request at any time by written notice of such withdrawal to the Host Transmission
      Owner and the Transmission Provider. Host Transmission Owner will complete the HLCS
      and issue a HILL Load Connection Report to the Transmission Customer and Transmission
      Provider by or before ninety (90) Calendar Days after receipt of an executed HLCS
      agreement, deposit and necessary data, or at a later date as the Parties mutually agree.


      Upon completion of the HLCS, the Network Customer or Transmission Customer must
 reimburse Host Transmission Owner for the unpaid cost of the HLCS if the cost of the HLCS
exceeds the deposit. Host Transmission Owner must refund to the Network Customer or
Transmission Customer any portion of the deposit that exceeds the cost of the HLCS with
interest earned in the interest-bearing account in which Host Transmission Owner has placed
the deposit, or if such account does not exist, with interest calculated in accordance with 18
C.F.R. § 35.19a(a)(2).


2.2       Transmission System Study: Upon receipt of the Request for a HDPLA, the
Transmission Provider will perform an assessment of the impact of the requested delivery
point configuration change on the Transmission System and, if requested by the Network
Customer or Transmission Customer, information detailing the limitations of the
Transmission System in supporting any Conditional High Impact Large Load Service. The
Transmission Provider will conclude its assessment and notify the Transmission Customer of
the findings. All HILLs without Designated Resources or planned generation for any
megawatt amounts of requested transmission service of the HILL will be subject to the
HDPLA, described below, and to supplemental study requirements outlined in Section
2.1.3.4 of Attachment BA of this Tariff. During the HDPLA, Transmission Provider will
assess the impacts on the Transmission System caused by requested HILL delivery point
additions or modifications due to the increased load using power flow, short circuit,
dynamics, and any other analyses that are appropriate.


The Transmission Provider will send a study report to the Transmission Customer and the
Host Transmission Owner within ninety (90) Calendar Days of all Parties agreeing to study
assumptions during the scoping call. If the Transmission Provider is unable to complete the
study within ninety (90) Calendar Days, the Transmission Provider will notify the
Transmission Customer and the Host Transmission Owner and provide an estimate of the
time needed to reach a final determination along with an explanation of the reason(s) that
additional time is required to complete the study. Upon completion of the HDPLA, the
Transmission Customer must reimburse the Transmission Provider for the cost of the
HDPLA. The HDPLA study results do not establish a HILL delivery point without an
effective Service Agreement. A requirement for establishment of a HILL delivery point is
 the execution of a Service Agreement by the Transmission Customer or Network Customer
for that delivery point or Commission approval of such a Service Agreement if filed
unexecuted. Any portion of the HILL delivery point load that is to be served with firm
transmission service requires a Service Agreement pursuant to Part II or Part III of the Tariff.
Any portion of the HILL delivery point load that is to be served with CHILLS requires a
Service Agreement pursuant to Part VII of the Tariff. The HDPLA study results will expire
one (1) year after issuance of the study report.
